target.consumer: stale recovery allocator and 50-worker canary verifier

problem: A live canary incident on O-SWARM-KERNEL-IMPLEMENT-V1 produced two overlapping append-only recovery claims within roughly one minute. The later claim recorded overlapping_nonstale_recovery_found=false even though a prior nonstale recovery claim already existed. The earlier recovery critic had independently predicted this exact class as F3_RECOVERY_GENERATION_NO_FENCE. This is now observed falsification evidence, not only a theoretical risk: stale recovery has no atomically enforced per-opportunity active-generation fence, so concurrent recoverers can both become active.
acceptance: A live two-worker recovery race for one stale opportunity yields at most one active nonstale recovery generation and the loser deterministically observes the winner without overwriting.
Recovery eligibility rechecks active recovery claims under the latest host head immediately before create and create-if-absent fencing prevents a second active generation under concurrent starts.
Existing append-only recovery evidence and no-overwrite semantics remain preserved; stale timeout/retry rules and unrelated opportunities are unchanged.
A regression test reproduces the 2026-09-17 kernel double-recovery incident and fails without the fence and passes with it.
title: Fence concurrent stale-recovery generations
mission: Design, implement and canary an atomic per-opportunity recovery-generation fence so concurrent stale-recovery workers cannot both acquire active recovery authority, while preserving append-only recovery evidence, deterministic loser reconciliation and the existing stale/retry policy.

goal_relevance.reason: The universal-worker canary depends on safe stale recovery under many concurrent disposable workers; duplicate active recoverers directly violate useful parallelism and scoped mutation safety.

information_gain.reason: The observed kernel incident converts the recovery critic's previously hypothetical generation-fence failure into concrete live canary evidence with two durable conflicting recovery claims.

regression_prevention.reason: A deterministic concurrent-start test can turn this incident into an invariant: at most one active recovery generation per opportunity, with loser reconciliation preserved durably.

human_friction_reduction.reason: Preventing duplicate recoverers avoids requiring the human or guide to notice and arbitrate overlapping recovery attempts during mass /wc launches.

falsification: Two concurrent eligible recovery workers can both acquire active recovery authority for the same opportunity.
A loser can overwrite, supersede or mutate the winner's recovery claim rather than reconciling append-only.
The generation fence prevents recovery of a genuinely stale opportunity when no active nonstale recovery generation exists.
The repair changes the documented 20-minute suspicion or 30-minute recovery-eligibility thresholds without separate authority.
The regression test does not reproduce the durable 2026-09-17 kernel double-recovery shape before the repair.
dedup_note: The recovery critic already identified F3_RECOVERY_GENERATION_NO_FENCE, so this proposal does not duplicate that analysis. Its new durable value is the live 2026-09-17 kernel incident proving that two nonstale recovery generations were actually claimed and that the later worker failed to observe the earlier one. No inspected current proposal used this canonical root/target/problem/acceptance identity.
